question: What types of exception can be encountered in file handling? Write a program to create a class named MOVIE with data members name and genre. If the genre of the movie is comedy then write it to COMEDY.DAT and if the genre is action, write it to ACTION.DAT
answer:
In file handling, the following exceptions may be encountered:

  • File not found : When the specified file does not exist.
  • Permission denied : When the program does not have rights to access the file.
  • End of file (EOF) : When reading goes beyond the available data.
  • Disk full / write error : When there is not enough space to write.
  • Invalid file operation : When a wrong mode is used for opening the file.

    CODE:

    #include <iostream>
#include <fstream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

class MOVIE {
    string name;
    string genre;

public:
    void getData() {
        cout << "Enter movie name: ";
        getline(cin, name);
        cout << "Enter movie genre (comedy/action): ";
        getline(cin, genre);
    }

    void writeToFile() {
        try {
            if (genre == "comedy" || genre == "Comedy") {
                ofstream fout("COMEDY.DAT", ios::app);
                if (!fout)
                    throw "Error opening COMEDY.DAT";
                fout << "Name: " << name << ", Genre: " << genre << endl;
                fout.close();
            }
            else if (genre == "action" || genre == "Action") {
                ofstream fout("ACTION.DAT", ios::app);
                if (!fout)
                    throw "Error opening ACTION.DAT";
                fout << "Name: " << name << ", Genre: " << genre << endl;
                fout.close();
            }
            else {
                throw "Unknown genre!";
            }
        }
        catch (const char* msg) {
            cerr << "Exception: " << msg << endl;
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    MOVIE m;
    m.getData();
    m.writeToFile();
    cout << "Movie data saved successfully!" << endl;
    return 0;
}

question: Discuss the chain of constructor and destructor in derived class. Write a program to define a class named Employee with data members name, age and gender. Then create another class named EmployeeSalary inherited from Employee. In this class, the user should give the monthly salary of the employee and calculate the yearly salary after 15% tax deduction. In the main function, you should get the employee’s basic information and salary using inheritance.
answer:
In the case of inheritance, when an object of a derived class is created, the constructor of the base class is executed first, followed by the constructor of the derived class. This ensures that the base part of the object is properly initialized before the derived part. Similarly, during destruction, the order is reversed: first the destructor of the derived class is called and then the destructor of the base class. This mechanism guarantees that the resources of the derived class are released before the base class resources, maintaining proper construction and destruction order.

CODE:

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

class Employee {
protected:
    string name;
    int age;
    string gender;
public:
    Employee(string n, int a, string g) {
        name = n;
        age = a;
        gender = g;
        cout << "Employee constructor called" << endl;
    }
    ~Employee() {
        cout << "Employee destructor called" << endl;
    }
    void displayBasicInfo() {
        cout << "Name: " << name << endl;
        cout << "Age: " << age << endl;
        cout << "Gender: " << gender << endl;
    }
};

class EmployeeSalary : public Employee {
    float monthlySalary;
public:
    EmployeeSalary(string n, int a, string g, float ms) 
        : Employee(n, a, g) {
        monthlySalary = ms;
        cout << "EmployeeSalary constructor called" << endl;
    }
    ~EmployeeSalary() {
        cout << "EmployeeSalary destructor called" << endl;
    }

    void calculateYearlySalary() {
        float yearly = monthlySalary * 12;
        float netSalary = yearly - (0.15f * yearly);  // 15% tax deduction
        displayBasicInfo();
        cout << "Monthly Salary: " << monthlySalary << endl;
        cout << "Yearly Salary after 15% tax: " << netSalary << endl;
    }
};

int main() {
    string name, gender;
    int age;
    float salary;

    cout << "Enter name: ";
    getline(cin, name);
    cout << "Enter age: ";
    cin >> age;
    cout << "Enter gender: ";
    cin >> gender;
    cout << "Enter monthly salary: ";
    cin >> salary;

    EmployeeSalary emp(name, age, gender, salary);
    emp.calculateYearlySalary();

    return 0;
}

question: When do we use static member functions? Explain the types of constructors with an example.
answer:
Static member functions are used when we want a function of a class to access only the static data members of that class. They do not operate on individual objects, so they cannot access non-static data members directly. We use them when:

  • We need to manipulate static variables that are shared by all objects of the class.
  • We want a function to be callable without creating an object, using ClassName::functionName().

The types of constructors are:-

  1. Default Constructor: A constructor with no arguments, used to initialize objects with default values.
  2. Parameterized Constructor: A constructor that takes arguments to initialize objects with specific values.
  3. Copy Constructor: A constructor that initializes one object as a copy of another existing object.

    Example:

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Student {
    string name;
    int age;
public:
    // Default Constructor
    Student() {
        name = "Unknown";
        age = 0;
        cout << "Default constructor called" << endl;
    }

    // Parameterized Constructor
    Student(string n, int a) {
        name = n;
        age = a;
        cout << "Parameterized constructor called" << endl;
    }

    // Copy Constructor
    Student(const Student &s) {
        name = s.name;
        age = s.age;
        cout << "Copy constructor called" << endl;
    }

    void display() {
        cout << "Name: " << name << ", Age: " << age << endl;
    }
};

int main() {
    Student s1;              // Default constructor
    s1.display();

    Student s2("Ram", 20);   // Parameterized constructor
    s2.display();

    Student s3(s2);          // Copy constructor
    s3.display();

    return 0;
}

question: Write a function template that returns the greater number between two integers.
answer:
A function template allows us to write a single function that works with different data types.
Function template that returns the greater number between two integers is given below:

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

// Function template
template <class T>
T getGreater(T a, T b) {
    if (a > b)
        return a;
    else
        return b;
}

int main() {
    int x = 10, y = 20;
    cout << "Greater number is: " << getGreater(x, y) << endl;

    return 0;
}

question: Describe the characteristics of object oriented programming approach.
answer:
The main characteristics of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) are:

  1. Encapsulation: Wrapping of data and functions into a single unit (class), which hides internal details and exposes only necessary information.
  2. Abstraction: Showing only essential features of an object while hiding unnecessary implementation details.
  3. Inheritance: The ability of a class (derived) to acquire properties and behavior of another class (base), promoting reusability.
  4. Polymorphism: The ability of an object or function to take multiple forms, such as function overloading, operator overloading, and virtual functions.
  5. Modularity and Reusability: Programs are divided into small, manageable classes and objects which can be reused in different applications.

question: Write a program to create a class PERSON with data members name and age. Overload the greater than (>) symbol, to display the name of elder one.
answer:
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

class PERSON {
    string name;
    int age;
public:
    PERSON(string n, int a) {
        name = n;
        age = a;
    }

    // Overloading > operator
    bool operator>(PERSON p) {
        return (age > p.age);
    }

    string getName() {
        return name;
    }
};

int main() {
    PERSON p1("Ram", 25);
    PERSON p2("Shyam", 30);

    if (p1 > p2)
        cout << "Elder: " << p1.getName() << endl;
    else
        cout << "Elder: " << p2.getName() << endl;

    return 0;
}

question: Define virtual base class. Differentiate between function overloading and function overriding.
answer:
A virtual base class is a class that is declared as virtual when used in multiple inheritance to avoid multiple copies of the base class in the derived class. It ensures that only one shared copy of the base class exists in the inheritance hierarchy, preventing ambiguity (diamond problem).

The differences between function overloading and function overloading are:-

Feature Function Overloading Function Overriding
Definition Same function name with different parameters in the same class Redefining a base class function in a derived class with the same signature
Parameters Must differ (number/type of parameters) Must be same as base class function
Return Type Can be different Must be same (or compatible in some cases)
Inheritance Happens within the same class Requires inheritance (base & derived)
Compile/Run Time Resolved at compile time (Compile-time Polymorphism) Resolved at runtime using virtual function (Run-time Polymorphism)

question: What types of instructions are written in try block? Illustrate the use of friend function with an example.
answer:
The try block contains instructions that may cause exceptions during program execution, such as:

    1. Division by zero
    2. File handling operations (open/read/write)
    3. Array index out of bounds
    4. Dynamic memory allocation errors

Essentially, any statement that might throw an exception is placed inside the try block.

A friend function is a function not a member of a class but can access private and protected members of that class.

Second part:

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Box {
private:
    double length;
public:
    Box(double l) { length = l; }

    // Friend function declaration
    friend void showLength(Box b);
};

// Friend function definition
void showLength(Box b) {
    cout << "Length of the box is: " << b.length << endl;
}

int main() {
    Box b1(10.5);
    showLength(b1);  // Accesses private member via friend function
    return 0;
}

question: Create a class BOOK with data members name and price. Write a member function that will take two objects of BOOK class and return the object with lower price.
answer:
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

class BOOK {
    string name;
    float price;

public:
    // Constructor
    BOOK(string n = "", float p = 0.0) {
        name = n;
        price = p;
    }

    // Member function to compare two BOOK objects
    BOOK getLowerPrice(BOOK b) {
        if (price < b.price)
            return *this;  // Return current object
        else
            return b;      // Return passed object
    }

    void display() {
        cout << "Book Name: " << name << ", Price: " << price << endl;
    }
};

int main() {
    BOOK b1("C++ Programming", 500);
    BOOK b2("Python Programming", 450);

    BOOK cheaper = b1.getLowerPrice(b2);
    cout << "Book with lower price:" << endl;
    cheaper.display();

    return 0;
}

question: Design a class TIME with hour and minutes. Write a program to convert integer type to TIME class type.
answer:
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class TIME {
    int hour;
    int minutes;

public:
    // Default constructor
    TIME() {
        hour = 0;
        minutes = 0;
    }

    // Parameterized constructor
    TIME(int h, int m) {
        hour = h;
        minutes = m;
    }

    void display() {
        cout << "Time: " << hour << " hours " << minutes << " minutes" << endl;
    }

    // Conversion from int to TIME (constructor)
    TIME(int totalMinutes) {
        hour = totalMinutes / 60;
        minutes = totalMinutes % 60;
    }
};

int main() {
    int totalMinutes;
    cout << "Enter total minutes: ";
    cin >> totalMinutes;

    TIME t = totalMinutes;  // int to TIME conversion
    t.display();

    return 0;
}

question: Illustrate the advantage of return by reference with an example.
answer:
The advantages of return by reference are as follows:-

  • Returning by reference allows the function to return the actual object (or variable) rather than a copy.
  • This avoids copying overhead, which is efficient for large objects.
  • It also allows modification of the original object directly through the returned reference.

    Example:-

    #include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Number {
    int value;
public:
    Number(int v) { value = v; }

    // Function returning reference
    int& getValue() {
        return value;
    }

    void display() {
        cout << "Value: " << value << endl;
    }
};

int main() {
    Number n1(10);

    cout << "Original value:" << endl;
    n1.display();

    // Modifying value using returned reference
    n1.getValue() = 50;

    cout << "After modifying through reference:" << endl;
    n1.display();

    return 0;
}
